excerpts: Hubbard helps the Panthers top the Saints, 20-17, and retain first place in the NFC South By AP Updated: Nov 15, 2026, 11:41 pm Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email NEW ORLEANS -- — [Chuba Hubbard](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4241416/chuba-hubbard) made long gains out of short passes, pushed through tacklers and pulled the mistake-prone [Carolina Panthers](http://www.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/car/carolina-panthers) out of a three-game slide. Hubbard gained 172 yards from scrimmage and ran for two touchdowns, and [Ryan Fitzgerald](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4568263/ryan-fitzgerald) 's 54-yard field goal as time expired lifted Carolina to a 20-17 victory over the [New Orleans Saints](http://www.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/no/new-orleans-saints) on Sunday with the NFC South Division lead at stake.

excerpts: Hubbard rushed for 92 yards on 27 carries, and also gained 80 yards on five catches for Carolina (4-5), which won despite committing a franchise-record 17 penalties for 152 yards. The Saints (3-6) by contrast, were flagged just three times, but the last cost them the game less than 30 seconds after [Charlie Smyth](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/5208518/charlie-smyth) had hit a 55-yard field goal to tie it at 17. Saints coach Kellen Moore withheld criticism of the officials, noting that the Saints, on balance, benefitted from penalty calls. “We had plenty of opportunities in this game," Moore said. “We didn’t get it done.” While both teams entered the game with losing records, the winner was going to take the lead of their anemic division, which Carolina won in 2025 with an 8-9 record.

excerpts: Carolina, which led 7-0 at halftime, was up just 10-7 when [Alvin Kamara](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/3054850/alvin-kamara) 's 4-yard touchdown catch gave New Orleans a 14-10 lead with 3:49 left. [Bryce Young](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4685720/bryce-young) responded with short passes to Hubbard for gains of 29 and 34 yards to set up the work-horse running back's second short TD run, putting Carolina back in front with 1:49 left. “He’s the heart and soul of everything we do,” Young said of Hubbard. “I just wanted to get it into a special player’s hands.” Saints quarterback [Tyler Shough](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4360689/tyler-shough) , who was intercepted and lost a fumble during the game, drove New Orleans into position for Smyth's tying field goal with 41 seconds left. Young finished 17 of 30 passing for 200 yards without a turnover. Shough was 25 of 35 for 187 yards. Saints rookie receiver [Jordyn Tyson](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4880281/jordyn-tyson) caught 11 passes for 80 yards. But the Saints struggled to run the ball despite the return of Tavis Etienne from injured reserve. Etienne gained just 14 yards on eight carries and New Orleans finished with just 49 yards rushing.

recap.paragraph: Ryan Fitzgerald kicked a 54-yard field goal as time ran out! The Panthers beat the Saints 20-17 in New Orleans. Earlier, Alvin Kamara caught a touchdown to put the Saints ahead. Chuba Hubbard ran for a score to put Carolina back on top. Charlie Smyth tied it with a 55-yard kick, setting up Fitzgerald's big moment. The victory ended Carolina's 3-game slide and kept the Panthers in first place in the NFC South.
